title: CEO Interview with David Reeder from Entegris - Semiwiki
gist: Entegris CEO David Reeder positions the company as a leading-edge semiconductor materials supplier whose content grows with AI-driven complexity in advanced logic, HBM, EUV and advanced packaging, where customers qualify materials years ahead of volume production and buy on yield and total cost of ownership rather than price. Concrete disclosures include a metal-oxide EUV resist patent cross-license with JSR and Inpria, a Colorado Springs Manufacturing Center of Excellence, a Korea Technology Center in Ansan, and an IPA trace-metal contamination fix for an HBM customer.

insights.claim: Entegris frames AI as structurally increasing the materials intensity of chipmaking — more complex architectures raise the bar for purity, process control and reliability, meaning consumable-materials revenue should scale faster than wafer starts alone.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Supports a per-wafer content-growth thesis for materials/consumables suppliers rather than pure unit-volume exposure to fab capex.
insights.quote: That increases materials intensity and raises the bar for purity, process control, and reliability.
insights.locator: AI training, inference, and edge applications

insights.claim: The strongest application areas are advanced logic, high-performance memory, EUV and advanced packaging — i.e. Entegris revenue mix is levered to the leading edge rather than to trailing-node or broad-based silicon.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Leading-edge concentration means results should track TSMC/Samsung/SK hynix leading-node and HBM ramps more than aggregate semi units.
insights.quote: Our strongest application areas are tied to where the industry is moving fastest: advanced logic, high-performance memory, EUV, advanced packaging, and other high-performance applications enabled by AI.
insights.locator: What application areas are your strongest?

insights.claim: Near-term momentum is concentrated in advanced technologies while IoT, robotics, industrial automation, LEO satellites and electrification are cast as slower-burning long-term demand support — an implicit admission that the non-AI end markets are not currently the growth driver.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Watch for a broadening cycle: a recovery in industrial/auto silicon would be incremental upside on top of the AI-led base.
insights.quote: The near-term momentum is clearly strongest in advanced technologies, but the broader direction is consistent: more complexity, more critical materials, and a greater need for trusted technical partners.

insights.claim: Advanced-node materials are bought on reliability, yield impact, process stability and total cost of ownership rather than purchase price, which insulates qualified materials suppliers from price-led competition.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Implies durable gross margins and low price elasticity for incumbents; a bear case would require yield failures, not undercutting on price.
insights.quote: Customers evaluate materials based on reliability, yield impact, process stability, and total cost of ownership, not simply purchase price.
insights.locator: What does the competitive landscape look like

insights.claim: The chief risk Entegris sells against is variability: a single contamination event, materials inconsistency or process-control disruption can hit yield, slow ramps and add cost as nodes shrink.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Frames the value proposition as insurance against ramp delay — spend on materials scales with the cost of a failed ramp, which rises with node complexity.
insights.quote: The more advanced chips become, the less room there is for variability.

insights.claim: The semiconductor materials space is described as 'increasingly consilidated' [sic], signalling an ongoing M&A/consolidation dynamic among materials suppliers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Consolidation supports pricing power for scaled players and flags materials sub-scale names as potential acquisition targets.
insights.quote: The semiconductor materials space is highly competitive, differentiated, and increasingly consilidated, but success is ultimately earned in the fab.
insights.locator: What does the competitive landscape look like

insights.claim: Customers engage Entegris years before commercialization, while device and process roadmaps are still being shaped, so materials selection is locked in during qualification long before high-volume manufacturing revenue appears.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Creates multi-year revenue visibility and high switching costs, but also means today's design wins only monetize several nodes out — track qualification announcements as the leading indicator.
insights.quote: Customers often engage with us early—usually years before commercialization—when device and process roadmaps are still being shaped.
insights.locator: How do customers normally engage with your company?

insights.claim: A named case study involved trace metal contamination in IPA chemistries affecting a customer's HBM production, with Entegris developing the remediation — evidence that high-purity wet chemistries are a live yield bottleneck in HBM manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Points to HBM purity requirements as a specific pull for high-purity chemistry and filtration content per wafer as memory makers scale HBM capacity.
insights.quote: A good example is our response to a customer that was concerned about trace metal contamination in IPA chemistries affecting HBM production.
insights.locator: A good example is our response

insights.claim: Customer priorities reduce to three variables — ramp speed, yield and resiliency — which is the demand framework materials suppliers are being scored on.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A useful checklist for evaluating any fab-consumables vendor's pitch and for reading fab operators' procurement behavior.
insights.quote: Customer conversations tend to center on three priorities: ramp speed, yield, and resiliency.
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

themes.theme: EUV resist IP and photoresist roadmap

insights.claim: Entegris has struck an agreement with JSR Corporation and Inpria Corporation to cross-license metal oxide resist patents and explore collaboration on future photoresist materials, positioning it in the metal-oxide EUV resist IP pool.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Metal-oxide resists are the contested next-gen EUV/High-NA patterning material; cross-licensing removes IP friction and puts Entegris into a high-value, IP-gated segment alongside JSR/Inpria.
insights.quote: Our recent agreement with JSR Corporation and Inpria Corporation to cross-license metal oxide resist patents and explore collaborative opportunities for future photoresist materials

insights.claim: As EUV scales into higher-volume production, materials performance and consistency become more important rather than less — implying EUV consumable content per layer rises with EUV layer count.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Ties Entegris' EUV-linked revenue to ASML EUV tool utilization and to EUV layer counts at 2nm and below, not just to tool shipments.
insights.quote: As EUV scales into higher-volume production, materials performance and consistency become even more important.

insights.claim: Entegris is building a Manufacturing Center of Excellence in Colorado Springs to expand domestic U.S. production of critical products, an explicit onshoring of materials supply alongside U.S. fab construction.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Domestic materials capacity is a prerequisite for U.S. fab ramps; watch it as a capex line and as exposure to U.S. semiconductor policy support.
insights.quote: Our Manufacturing Center of Excellence in Colorado Springs strengthens U.S. semiconductor infrastructure and expands domestic production for critical products.
insights.locator: We are also investing in capabilities

insights.claim: A Korea Technology Center in Ansan is designed to simulate customer fab environments and support flexible cleanroom testing, placing qualification infrastructure next to Korean memory makers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Signals a deliberate push at Korean memory/HBM customers; co-located qualification labs shorten design-in cycles and defend share against local suppliers.
insights.quote: Our Korea Technology Center in Ansan is designed to simulate customer fab environments and support flexible cleanroom testing.
insights.locator: We are also investing in capabilities

insights.claim: In Taiwan and other critical semiconductor regions the stated strategy is to strengthen local capabilities and supplier ecosystems so customers get continuity of supply — i.e. customers are now buying geographic redundancy, not just materials.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Regionalization is a cost line and a moat at once: suppliers unable to fund duplicated regional footprints risk designed-out status as fabs multi-region.
insights.quote: In Taiwan and other critical semiconductor regions, our strategy is to strengthen local capabilities and supplier ecosystems so customers can count on continuity of supply and technical support where they need it most.
insights.locator: We have also invested around the world

insights.claim: Customers expanding manufacturing across regions specifically demand suppliers that deliver global consistency with strong local support, a requirement that favors scaled multinational materials vendors over regional specialists.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A structural argument for share gain by the largest materials platforms as fab footprints fragment geographically.
insights.quote: They are also expanding manufacturing across regions, which creates a need for suppliers that can provide global consistency with strong local support.
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

insights.claim: David Reeder became Entegris president and CEO in 2025 after serving as CFO of Chewy and, before that, CFO of GlobalFoundries where he led what was then the largest semiconductor IPO ever; he has been an Entegris director since March 2024 and joined Celestica's board in May 2026.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A finance-first CEO with IPO and supply-chain background raises the odds of portfolio reshaping, capital-structure action or M&A at Entegris; his Celestica board seat is a fresh AI-hardware linkage.
insights.quote: David Reeder became president and CEO of Entegris in 2025, with more than 20 years of semiconductor expertise across IDMs, fabless, foundry, systems, and component companies.
insights.locator: David Reeder became president and CEO

insights.claim: Reeder left the Alphawave Semi board in December 2025 after serving from September 2023, a directorship change disclosed alongside his other board roles.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Minor governance datapoint; relevant only for tracking board turnover around Alphawave Semi.
insights.quote: He was formerly a director of Alphawave Semi from September 2023 until December 2025.
insights.locator: Dave has served as a director
